name: Concert Flute
shortDescription: Silver transverse flute producing pure, clear tones via an air jet striking the embouchure hole edge.
description: The flute is a transverse (side-blown) aerophone producing sound through an edge tone: the player directs a focused air jet across the embouchure hole's sharp inner edge, creating alternating vortices above and below the aperture. This oscillation excites the air column to resonate at pitches determined by the open key holes. Unlike reed instruments, the flute has no vibrating solid, making its tone closest to a pure sine wave in the lower register.
historicalOrigins: Flutes are among the oldest musical instruments (bone flutes from 43,000 BCE). The modern Boehm system flute was developed by Theobald Boehm in Munich in 1847.
acousticPrinciples: Edge tone: air jet strikes lip plate edge creating alternating vortex shedding above/below
Vortex frequency locks to tube resonance frequency — the jet oscillates synchronously with the air column
Open cylindrical bore: overblows at the octave (2nd harmonic); supports even and odd partials
Key hole closure truncates effective tube length; all-keys-closed = lowest pitch (B3/C4)

characteristics.pitchRange: C4 (261.6 Hz) to C7 (2093 Hz); some extend to B3
characteristics.timbralColor: Pure, airy, clear in low register; bright and penetrating in high register
characteristics.orchestralRole: Soprano melodic voice, orchestral colour, solo virtuosity, piccolo-range

soundDNA.exciter: Focused air jet across embouchure hole sharp edge — aeroacoustic edge tone
soundDNA.resonator: Open cylindrical silver bore with tone holes
soundDNA.harmonics: Near-sinusoidal in low register; 2nd and 3rd harmonics grow with register
soundDNA.attackDecay: Soft attack controlled by air jet angle; sustained while blown
soundDNA.timbreProfile: Pure clear fundamental low register; brighter and richer in upper registers
soundDNA.radiationPattern: Primarily from open tone holes closest to the embouchure; directional at high frequencies

headjoint.label: Headjoint & Embouchure
headjoint.function: Head joint contains embouchure hole where player focuses the air jet to create the edge tone.

characteristics.material: Silver, gold, or platinum tube with lip plate and riser
characteristics.mechanism: Air jet vortex across sharp inner edge of embouchure hole
characteristics.role: Primary tone generation via edge-tone oscillation

body.label: Main Body
body.function: Cylindrical bore housing the majority of tone holes and key mechanisms.

characteristics.material: Silver-plated nickel-silver or solid silver tube
characteristics.mechanism: Open cylindrical bore resonator — overblows at octave
characteristics.role: Air column resonator and pitch selection

keywork.label: Boehm Key System
keywork.function: 15+ padded key cups on rods covering tone holes. Plateau or open-hole variants available.

characteristics.material: Silver-plated nickel-silver keys with cork or synthetic pads
characteristics.mechanism: Pad closure seals tone hole changing effective tube length

footjoint.label: Footjoint
footjoint.function: Detachable foot extends range to C4 (C-foot) or B3 (B-foot).

characteristics.material: Silver-plated nickel-silver with C or B rollers
characteristics.mechanism: Two or three additional key mechanisms for lowest notes

followTheSound.title: Edge-Tone Excitation
followTheSound.explanation: Air jet oscillates across the embouchure hole edge at the tube's resonant frequency.

followTheSound.title: Pitch Selection
followTheSound.explanation: Open/closed key pads determine the effective tube length (L) and therefore the resonant pitch.

followTheSound.title: Cylindrical Resonance
followTheSound.explanation: Cylindrical bore resonates at half-wavelengths. Overblowing opens the second harmonic (octave).

followTheSound.title: Low Register Extension
followTheSound.explanation: Footjoint keys extend the air column, enabling the lowest notes of the instrument.
